assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a boson with Higgs-like properties completed the Standard Model's electroweak sector and is one of the most consequential experimental results in modern physics. Detector conception, construction and the two independent analyses are decisive, and the result has been followed by sustained coupling and spin-parity measurements.
assessment.attribution: The 2013 prize went to the theorists, leaving the experimental discovery unrecognized. Credit sits with the founding leadership of ATLAS and CMS; a three-person cap forces a choice among four credited names, and I propose two ATLAS and one CMS founding spokesperson, which is a judgement call that omits Tejinder S. Virdee and leaves the balance between the two experiments contestable. Thousands of collaborators contributed, and any laureate configuration is partly a recognition of leadership.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: independent confirmation by two experiments since 2012, combined Run 1 and Run 2 coupling measurements consistent with the Standard Model, and a stable interpretation. Recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Collaboration-scale discovery makes individual attribution inherently unsatisfactory under the three-laureate limit.
Whether the committee regards the 2013 theory prize as having already settled this topic is a matter of committee judgement I cannot verify.
My recollection of each person's exact role (spokesperson terms, detector design) is from general knowledge and not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks combine the magic-wavelength trapping idea with large ensembles of atoms interrogated at the 1e-18 level. They have redefined the frontier of precision measurement, enabling tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a path to redefining the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and demonstrated early strontium clocks; Ye's group drove the performance to record accuracy and many-body-clock physics. This is a clean two-person configuration well supported by the credited names. Other contributors such as Pierre Lemonde and Hidetoshi Katori's competitors are not in the credited list, so I do not propose them.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent laboratories (strontium, ytterbium) reproduce 1e-18 performance, intercomparisons exist, and the redefinition of the second is being prepared. Timing is good, though the 2005 prize already recognised frequency combs.
uncertainties: Overlap with prior prizes on laser spectroscopy and ion clocks may be weighed against it.
The precise division of priority among groups for the lattice-clock concept is from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum matter, a new platform for tunable correlated electrons that has launched a large new subfield with a clear prediction-then-experiment arc.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model supplied the theory and the Cao et al. experiments in Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the discovery. This theory-experiment pairing fits a three-person prize well. The first author of the experimental work, Yuan Cao, is a junior contributor not in the credited names, and the role of earlier twisted-graphene work is not fully resolved in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature but young, about eight years since the experiments: the correlated-insulator and superconducting phases are widely reproduced, though the microscopic pairing mechanism is still debated. Recognition would be somewhat early but defensible.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains unsettled.
Possible earlier or parallel priority claims for twisted-bilayer theory are not established by the supplied text.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for application impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators reframed band theory through topological invariants and protected edge states. The theoretical proposal and the HgTe experimental realisation form a complete discovery with a lasting influence across condensed matter, photonics and quantum materials.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele introduced the Z2 classification and the spin Hall proposal in graphene; Molenkamp's group observed the effect in HgTe quantum wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. This ballot entry lists the cleanest three-name configuration. Shoucheng Zhang, a key theorist, is deceased and Bernevig and Hughes are not among the credited names, so attribution omits an important prediction step.
assessment.maturity: Mature: the effect is confirmed in several material families, and 3D topological insulators were confirmed by ARPES. Overlapping with the 2016 topological-phase prize, which recognised the theoretical framework of a different class of phases, is a possible objection.
uncertainties: The 2016 prize on topological phases may reduce appetite for a further topology prize.
Omission of the BHZ prediction and of 3D topological insulator work in the credited names leaves attribution incomplete.
Overlap with a separate ballot entry listing quantum anomalous Hall work is a bundling question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics is the architecture behind essentially all superconducting quantum processors: strong coupling of a qubit to a microwave resonator gives dispersive readout, qubit coupling and a route to error-corrected devices. It is a foundational idea with major impact on quantum technology.
assessment.attribution: The 2004 proposal and first strong-coupling demonstration are credited to Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf with their coauthors; Steven Girvin and others are not in the credited names, so the three-person set may omit parties with fair claims. As a member whose own work is in this field and who directs WACQT at Chalmers, I note a close subject-matter link and a likely need for conflict disclosure, and I have tried to rank it on merit, which argues for placing it below clearly independent candidates.
assessment.maturity: Mature as an experimental platform, with wide replication and commercial processors. However, the 2025 prize already honoured macroscopic quantum effects in circuits, so recognition now might be viewed as too close in time and subject.
uncertainties: Disclosure of my own Chalmers and WACQT links to this area; a conservative ranking reflects that.
The 2025 prize may be seen as having covered this territory partially.
The credited trio may not capture all decisive contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with tunable parameters, enabling the Mott-insulator transition and quantum gas microscopy, with growing impact on quantum simulation of many-body systems.
assessment.attribution: Zoller supplied the Hubbard-model proposal with collaborators, Greiner the Mott-insulator observation and Bloch the broad platform development; Esslinger, among the four credited, led the fermionic Hubbard work. Limiting to three leaves out Tilman Esslinger and the proposal's co-authors, so the allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a platform with independent groups and many results, though large-scale simulation of open problems such as the 2D Hubbard phase diagram is still developing. Prior cold-atom prizes (1997, 2001) may reduce urgency.
uncertainties: Allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger and Zoller is difficult.
Overlap with the closely related controlled-atom candidate on the same longlist.
Whether quantum simulation has delivered a decisive new physical discovery rather than a platform.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the association with the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies, a distinct new messenger.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the project; Karle and Spiering are central in design, construction and leadership. The credited names give a plausible trio, but collaboration-scale effort again makes individual credit imperfect and early pioneers of neutrino astronomy are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature: the diffuse flux is firmly established and independently supported, while source identification is still limited to a few associations. Further confirmation by KM3NeT or other detectors would strengthen timing.
uncertainties: Source association evidence remains statistically modest.
Neutrino astronomy was partly honoured in 2002; overlap is possible.
My knowledge of the latest source-identification results is incomplete.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of the M87 and Sgr A* shadows are a striking, direct test of strong-field general relativity and demonstrate global VLBI at 1.3 mm. The result is a major observational achievement of broad public and scientific interest.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, Doeleman led the EHT, and Zensus led the European effort. The collaboration is very large and the credited names are leaders rather than sole inventors, so credit allocation is not fully clean.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature with Sgr A* following M87*, but interpretations of the ring (spin, jet, plasma models) are still evolving and the black hole subject was recognised in 2017 and 2020, so timing might be debated.
uncertainties: Ring interpretation depends on modelling assumptions.
Precedent of recent black-hole prizes.
Leadership-based credit versus invention.
